expectedRealization.rationale: The statutory change starts immediately after cutoff, but heterogeneous pass-through prevents a generic earnings horizon.

changeHypothesis.summary: The manufacturing VAT rate was cut from 16% to 13% effective April 1, but economic benefit depends on invoice pricing, pass-through, supplier/customer bargaining and tax-credit structure rather than automatically becoming issuer profit.
changeHypothesis.persistenceReason: The tax-rate change is structural, but the direction and magnitude of company earnings transmission are heterogeneous.
disconfirmingEvidence: A VAT cut can be passed through to customers.
Different industries have different input/output VAT structures.
No coherent company subset with a frozen direct retained-margin bridge was established.

selectionComparison.rationale: No listed expression meets the frozen earnings-conversion and expectation-gap requirements.

expectations.marketExpectationAtCutoff: The April 1 tax cut was publicly announced before cutoff and broadly discussed across manufacturing.
expectations.thesisExpectation: Selection requires evidence that a specific company retains a material portion of the tax benefit rather than passing it through.
expectations.measurableGap: No measurable company-specific retained-margin expectation gap is frozen.

hypothesisDecompositionTest.rationale: Different pricing-power/input-credit structures imply opposite earnings effects; without verified subgroups the aggregate cannot support selection.

nearTerm.driver: tax rate changes immediately but price contracts/pass-through vary

mediumTerm.driver: margin/cash benefit depends on company-specific pricing power

structural.driver: lower statutory VAT burden can improve economic efficiency but not necessarily issuer margin

evidenceHorizonMatrix.resolutionRule: Split by pricing power and input/output VAT structure before any company mapping; unresolved aggregate remains No selection.

leaderDivergenceTest.rationale: No company-specific retained-benefit evidence is frozen.

bearCase: Competitive pass-through transfers most of the tax reduction to customers, leaving little incremental profit.
nextResearchActions: No selection; future research must decompose by pricing power instead of buying a generic VAT-cut theme.
